lesson: Recent reporting explicitly framed Shreyas Iyer and Sanju Samson as the captaincy race, but the forecast still put 55 percent on Samson and only 22 percent on Iyer. When credible reporting presents two co-frontrunners without a direct selector signal, keep their probabilities much closer and avoid pushing either above 50 percent.

The forecast identified the correct person but used the transliteration Falih al-Fayyadh, which the harness did not normalize. For source-driven named-person questions, copy the canonical spelling used by the likely resolving article rather than substituting a familiar transliteration.

Assigning 75 percent to Ange-Yoan Bonny was far too concentrated for a friendly's winning-goal market with many plausible attackers. Even with a lineup or narrative cue, keep scorer distributions broad; Amad Diallo was included but severely underweighted at 6 percent.

The institution mapping was correct, and the harness accepted U.S. Department of State as equivalent to State Department. Ordinary institutional aliases appear safer than person-name transliteration variants, though exact source wording remains preferable.
